newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends higher again with US heating oil.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends higher again with US heating oil.

text.p: IPE Brent made fresh gains late on Thursday consolidating Wednesday's dollar a barrel leap and confirming the bulls have regained control of the market.
U.S. heating oil again led the way and January Brent finished up 26 cents at $23.60 a barrel. The expiring December contract ended down four cents at $23.85 as traders rolled forward long positions.
Markets held gains after U.S. inventory statistics, as anticipated, showed a halt in the recent build in depleted distillate stocks.
"The stats came in on the mark and apart from a little profit taking on NYMEX early on that was enough to maintain the momentum," said an IPE broker.
Falling temperatures in the U.S. northeast and northwest Europe also helped underpin the renewed rally.
Earlier December IPE gas oil ended up $3.00 a tonne at $219.25 but well below the day's high of $223.00.
"Gas oil shot its bolt first thing this morning," said Alastair Harris of brokers MeesPierson.
Traders said uncertainty over the possible effects of Tuesday's record 865,100 tonne delivery into the expired November gas oil contract was still hanging over the market.

Some traders say the player believed to be due to take most the material will have no trouble placing it, while the bears argue that the massive delivery could result in oversupply in the key Rotterdam market.
Other dealers remained bullish on European gas oil fundamentals, pointing to a Turkish tender to buy 100,000 tonnes for December. In November it bought 225,000 tonnes.
